title: Version Control Concepts and Why Git Matters
learning_objectives: Explain what version control is and why it's essential for software development
Describe the key problems version control solves (collaboration, history, experimentation)
Understand the difference between centralized and distributed version control systems
Articulate why Git is the industry standard and how it applies to CatchBook development
outline: Introduction: The problem of file chaos without version control
What is version control? Core concepts: snapshots, history, branches
Evolution of version control: CVS → SVN → Git
Centralized vs distributed version control systems
Why Git won: speed, branching, distributed nature, GitHub ecosystem
Real-world scenarios: solo projects, team collaboration, open source
CatchBook context: How Git will support your entire development journey
Checkpoint: Understanding the value of version control

catchbook_context.deliverable: Understanding why CatchBook needs Git from day 1

criteria: Can explain version control in your own words
Can identify 3 key problems version control solves
Can describe the difference between centralized and distributed VCS
Can explain why Git is chosen for CatchBook project

resources.title: Pro Git Book - Chapter 1: Getting Started
Git Tutorial for Beginners - What is Git?

professor_constraints: Use CatchBook examples throughout (e.g., tracking code changes for photo upload feature)
Keep explanations concrete, avoid abstract theory
Use analogies that resonate with building a real app
No hands-on coding in this lesson - pure concepts
Emphasize that Git is a tool, not an obstacle
Address common beginner fears (can't break things irreversibly)
